questions.statement: Which word is the auxiliary used for the simple future tense?
questions.context: Identifying the auxiliary for simple future.

options.feedback: Incorrect. This is for present tense.
Incorrect. This is for past tense.
Correct! "Will" is the auxiliary for future actions.
Incorrect. This is a form of the verb "to be".

questions.explanation:
The student identifies the basic auxiliary used to express future in English.

questions.statement: What is the common contraction of "will not"?

options.feedback: Incorrect spelling.
Correct! "Won't" is the contraction of "will not".
Incorrect. This is for "do not".
Incorrect. This is for "would not".

questions.explanation:
The student remembers the irregular negative contraction for the future auxiliary.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement:
Waiter: "What would you like to drink?"
Customer: "I ________ have a glass of orange juice, please."

options.feedback: Correct! We use "will" for spontaneous decisions made at the moment of speaking.
Incorrect. Missing "am" and usually used for pre-planned decisions.
Incorrect. You need an auxiliary or a different structure.
Incorrect. Past tense.

questions.explanation:
The student understands the use of "will" for spontaneous decisions in a communicative context.

---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: "Don't worry, Mom. I ________ help you with the cleaning tomorrow."

options.feedback: Incorrect. You need "will" for a promise.
Correct! "Will" is used for making promises.
Incorrect. This would be a promise NOT to help, which contradicts "Don't worry".
Incorrect. This is present tense.

questions.explanation:
The student understands the communicative function of "will" for making promises.

---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: "I think it ________ rain later this afternoon, so take an umbrella."

options.feedback: Incorrect. We don't use "to" after "will".
Correct! "Will" is used for predictions, especially with "I think".
Incorrect. If it won't rain, you don't need an umbrella.
Incorrect. Requires "going to" to form a future here.

questions.explanation:
The student applies the use of "will" for general predictions followed by logical advice.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: According to the text, what will happen in the year 2050?
questions.context:
A prediction about technology in the year 2050.
"In the future, robots will do most of the housework. We won't cook or clean anymore. Life will be much easier for everyone."

options.feedback: Incorrect. It says life will be "easier".
Correct! The text says robots "will do most of the housework".
Incorrect. It says "we won't cook".
Incorrect. The text says there will be robots.

questions.explanation:
The student applies reading strategies to identify specific future predictions in a short text.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: "Can you hear the phone? I ________ answer it!"

options.feedback: Correct! Spontaneous decision to answer the phone, using the contraction of "will".
Incorrect. Too long for a spontaneous decision and missing "to".
Incorrect. Contradicts the intention to answer.
Incorrect. No "to" after "will".

questions.explanation:
The student applies the contracted form of "will" in a common daily situation involving a spontaneous action.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which sentence expresses a spontaneous decision?
questions.context: Distinguishing between spontaneous decisions and existing plans.

options.text: I am going to travel to Cali next month.
options.feedback: Incorrect. This is a pre-planned intention.

options.text: We are going to have a party on Saturday.
options.feedback: Incorrect. This is a plan.

options.text: Oh, I forgot my wallet. I'll go back and get it.
options.feedback: Correct! The "Oh" signals a sudden realization and the "I'll" is the spontaneous decision.

options.text: He is going to be a doctor.
options.feedback: Incorrect. This is a long-term goal/intention.

questions.explanation:
The student analyzes different future structures to identify the specific use case for "will".

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: What is the consequence of not acting according to the scientist?
questions.context:
Analyzing an expert's prediction.
"The scientist believes that global temperatures will rise by 2 degrees in the next decade. If we don't act now, we will face many environmental problems."

options.feedback: Incorrect. They will rise.
Incorrect. We will "face" problems.
Correct! "Face many environmental problems" is the predicted outcome.
Incorrect. Contradicts the rise in temperature.

questions.explanation:
The student analyzes a cause-and-effect relationship expressed with future "will" in a scientific/environmental context.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which word best describes the tone of this speaker?
questions.context:
Evaluating a personal commitment.
"I promise I will never lie to you again. I'll always tell the truth, and I will support you in everything you do."

options.feedback: Incorrect. The tone is supportive and committed.
Correct! The use of "promise" and the repetition of "will" for commitment show sincerity.
Incorrect. These are strong commitments.
Incorrect. "Will" and "Never" show certainty in the commitment.

questions.explanation: The student evaluates the communicative intent and tone of a series of promises made using the future auxiliary "will".
